spec_match.rationale: Every program uses the exact shipped surfaces: requires buffer_view;, buffer / buffer<N> in var<storage>, bufferView<T>(ptr, offset), bufferArrayView<T>(ptr, offset, size), bufferLength(ptr) — names confirmed against Tint's BuiltinFn parsing and the proposal. The two negatives encode real spec contracts (opaque type not assignable; MinTypeSize(T) > N with const offset is a shader-creation error). A draft used the WGSL reserved word 'unsized' as an identifier; the real compiler caught it and it was renamed.

interactive.rationale: Program selector updates the displayed source and expectation line; Compile selected / Compile all six run real createShaderModule calls and render the raw getCompilationInfo messages per program. Verified via CDP: selecting program 5 and compiling produced exactly one result card with the real error.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The blurb promises six programs, real getCompilationInfo messages, and two must-fail-everywhere negatives — exactly what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers unsupported browsers (all six fail at line 1 with the real 'feature buffer_view is not supported'), missing adapter/device (distinct honest card message), negatives compiling cleanly (flagged as contradicting the spec and report-worthy), and positives failing while supported.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus 5094091886034944, feature page, and the proposal are linked.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite mirrors these six compiles one-to-one (four positives asserting zero errors, two negatives asserting errors>0) and the whole suite completed in this session's browser with the honest matrix: negatives pass, positives fail, listing fails.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 + SwiftShader (--enable-unsafe-webgpu --enable-features=Vulkan): all six programs compiled for real, each reporting [error] line 1:10 'feature buffer_view is not supported'; select+compile-selected driven via CDP; console clean after error-scoping createShaderModule. The success path (clean compiles, and the negatives' specific non-requires error messages) cannot be observed until a buffer_view-enabled build exists.

telemetry_health.rationale: bufferview-compile asserts expected-vs-observed per program only when the feature is listed; bufferview-compile-fallback fires separately for unsupported browsers and missing-device runs, so fallbacks never masquerade as passes.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; result cards use accent border-left (emerald/rose) with black text on ivory, comfortably AA; the primary buttons keep the global black/ivory pairing; focus-visible outlines set.

accessibility.rationale: Native select with a visible label, native buttons, status is an aria-live=polite output announcing the completion summary, results region carries an aria-label, and code samples are shown via textContent from the same string that compiles so screen-reader text matches reality. Individual result cards are appended without their own live region; the status summary is the announced surface.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360x740 DPR3: scrollWidth 360, full-page mobile screenshot read (controls stack to full width, cards wrap, pre scrolls in place); desktop 1280x2600 screenshot read. CLI 360 captures are inconclusive here due to the known headless min-width clamp, so CDP emulation was the check.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel layout without horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Flex-wrap control rows, full-width controls under a narrow breakpoint, and scroll containers for intrinsically wide content.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Controls wrap and go full-width under 640px; WGSL source sits in an overflow-x:auto pre; long inline code tokens break via overflow-wrap:anywhere; verified no page-level overflow at 360px.

guidanceConsulted.query: announce async operation result status live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce async outcomes through a polite live region tied to the triggering control's context.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The status output (aria-live=polite) announces the per-run summary including whether failures are the honest unsupported result.

openQuestions.title: Negative programs' supported-path error text unknown
openQuestions.detail: On a buffer_view-enabled build, programs 5 and 6 must fail with non-requires errors (non-assignable opaque type; MinTypeSize > N). The exact Tint message text has not been observed; re-run on Chrome 153+/Canary with unsafe WebGPU and record it.

openQuestions.title: popErrorScope result not surfaced in the UI
openQuestions.detail: Validation errors are captured via an error scope to keep the console clean, but only getCompilationInfo messages are rendered. Surfacing the popErrorScope GPUValidationError message as a second evidence line would make the page a fuller teaching tool.

summary: A real compile bench over the exact WGSL surfaces buffer_view ships, including two spec-contract negatives, with the honest unsupported result (the true Tint error at line 1:10) rendered per program in this session's Chromium 141 + SwiftShader. Its own draft bug — using the reserved word 'unsized' — was caught by the real compiler during verification and fixed, which is the point of compiling for real. Supported-path outputs remain to be recorded on a 153+ build.
